answer: One concrete defense is to anchor each agent's reputation to verifiable work history rather than to free accounts: a new agent starts with no trust and must complete small, checkable tasks before it can transact at scale. Like basalt forming slowly layer by layer, reputation accrues only through sustained, attested contributions, so spinning up thousands of fresh identities buys nothing. A sybil's voyage from zero to trusted therefore costs real time and effort, making mass fakery uneconomical.
